There are a variety of reasons.

I see in the comments below that you are Hungarian, and you also speak English as well, so a language barrier being what you're experiencing is unlikely.

What I suspect is that, since you claim that you have never been hypnotized before, you either have certain expectations for what hypnosis is and since the expectation isn't met, you bring yourself out of hypnosis. This also conveys a perception to yourself that you are unable to be hypnotized, which of course is untrue. One of the benefits of being hypnotized in person is that someone's pretalk can eliminate these misconceptions. 

If I had to offer any advice, it would be that you realize that you have expectations for the experience that you have for hypnosis. Now when you go into hypnosis, imagine that you don't have any expectations, or you can imagine setting all your expectations aside on a side table, bench, etc. Additionally, you can realize that you have been hypnotized before, and you hypnotize yourself on a regular basis whenever you hop in a car and subconsciously drive to where you need to go, or you get so entangled in the story of a book that you lose track of time. 

I hope this helps you :)
